---
title: 'spfungorum_gap'
description: 'Find species with Index Fungorum Brazil evidence that are missing from FFB'
toc: true
toc-depth: 3
---


```{r}
#| eval: false
fungaR::spfungorum_gap()
```

### Description

Given a fungal genus, cross-checks [Species
Fungorum](https://www.speciesfungorum.org) (Index Fungorum, maintained by the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew) against the
Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB) checklist to find species-level names that Index
Fungorum's own reported locality places in Brazil but that are not currently
registered in FFB. Like `mycobank_gap`, this is not a general diff
of the two databases: a name missing from FFB is only returned when Index Fungorum's
own locality data indicates it occurs in Brazil.

### Details

Species Fungorum/Index Fungorum has no bulk export, but it does publish a public,
documented web service (https://www.indexfungorum.org/ixfwebservice/fungus.asmx)
that answers plain HTTP GET requests with XML - no SOAP client, headless browser, or
authentication required, and no per-record page visit: a single request returns every
name matching `taxon`, including, for many records, the type specimen's own
reported `LOCATION` and `HOST` fields, which is what
`Fungorum_Brazil_Evidence` is derived from. Index Fungorum's `LOCATION`
field very often names a Brazilian state directly (e.g. `"Pernambuco"`) rather
than the country itself, so the check covers the country name and every Brazilian
state name (with or without diacritics), not just the literal word "Brazil".

A candidate counts as "already in FFB" if either its raw Index Fungorum name or its
Index Fungorum *currently accepted* name matches an FFB species - not the
current name alone - because Index Fungorum and FFB sometimes disagree on which genus
a name currently belongs to (the same situation documented for
`mycobank_gap`).

The FFB side of the comparison reuses `funga_get_children_taxa` to list
every species (accepted and synonym) currently registered in FFB for the requested
genus.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| taxon | Character. A single fungal genus name (e.g. `"Phellinotus"`). Species Fungorum's web service has no operation for searching by higher classification, so order-level searches are not supported. |
| require_brazil_evidence | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), the returned table is filtered to only the candidates whose Index Fungorum `Location` mentions Brazil (the country name or any Brazilian state) - i.e. names Index Fungorum itself indicates occur in Brazil but that FFB is still missing. Set to `FALSE` to instead return every Index Fungorum species-level name missing from FFB regardless of locality, with `Fungorum_Brazil_Evidence` alongside for manual review. |
| max_number | Numeric. Maximum number of matching names requested from the web service in a single call. Defaults to `1000`, generous for any genus. |
| version | Character. FFB dataset version to compare against. Defaults to `"latest"`. Passed to `funga_get_children_taxa`. |
| verbose | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), prints progress messages. |
| save | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), the result is saved to disk as an `.xlsx` spreadsheet. |
| dir | Character. Directory where the spreadsheet is saved when `save = TRUE`. Defaults to `"spfungorum_gap"`. |
| filename | Character. Name of the `.xlsx` file (without extension) to save. Defaults to `"spfungorum_gap_<taxon>"`. |
| html_report | Logical. If `TRUE` (default), also writes a self-contained HTML report (`<dir>/<filename>.html`) summarizing the results: KPI counts and the full candidate table as a sortable, filterable DT widget with buttons to copy or download it as CSV/Excel. Requires the rmarkdown, DT, and htmltools packages; if any is missing, the report is skipped with a message (the `.xlsx` spreadsheet is unaffected). |
| open_report | Logical. If `TRUE` (default in interactive sessions), opens the rendered HTML report in the default browser. |

### Value

A `data.frame`, one row per Index Fungorum species-level name found in
  the requested genus that is absent from the current FFB checklist and, by default,
  whose Index Fungorum locality data indicates it occurs in Brazil, with columns:

  Fungorum_NumberIndex Fungorum's numeric record identifier for the name.
  Taxon_nameThe binomial as registered in Index Fungorum.
  AuthorsAuthor citation.
  YearYear of publication.
  Name_statusIndex Fungorum's nomenclatural status (e.g. `"Legitimate"`).
  Current_nameIndex Fungorum's currently accepted name for this entry, when
    different (i.e. when `Taxon_name` is itself a synonym).
  Fungorum_Location, Fungorum_HostType specimen locality and host, as reported
    in Index Fungorum's own record (may be `NA` - not every record has these).
  Fungorum_URLDirect link to the name's Species Fungorum page.
  Fungorum_Brazil_EvidenceLogical; `TRUE` when `Fungorum_Location`
    mentions Brazil.
  In_FFBAlways `FALSE` (kept for clarity when combining with other tables).

### Examples

```r
# Index Fungorum species-level names for genus Phellinotus with a Brazilian
# reported locality that are still missing from FFB
gap <- spfungorum_gap(taxon = "Phellinotus")

# Every Index Fungorum name missing from FFB regardless of locality, for manual review
gap_all <- spfungorum_gap(taxon = "Phellinotus", require_brazil_evidence = FALSE)
```
